ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. blue
   C. run
   D. happiness

2. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

3. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

5. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

6. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the Library

7. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

8. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

10. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

11. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goed

12. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing – notices, posters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 14.5.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
